_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint or onboard --resume must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and FAILS CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `afi-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard re-copies the SOURCE manifest each --resume and the press source keeps `-pp-mcp`. The repo ships `afi-mcp`: the Makefile builds `bin/afi-mcp` and server.json's package identifier is `afi-mcp.mcpb`, so an `-pp-mcp` entry_point points at a binary that is never built (the MCP server fails to launch). No mechanical gate catches this (the build name and the manifest name are checked independently); the 4.24.0 re-vendor silently reverted the correct 0.1.0 value and CodeRabbit flagged it Critical on PR #100. See project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar.

handfixes.summary: channel_workflow.go `workflow archive` syncs the spec-derived `applications` resource, not an empty list
handfixes.why: The 4.24.0 reprint emitted `resources := []string{}` (empty) where afi 0.1.0 carried `[]string{"applications"}` and the sibling 4.24 connectors carry their own populated lists (acronis: clients/task-manager/..., connectwise-control: session_groups). An empty list makes `afi-cli workflow archive` a silent no-op (the registered command builds and runs but syncs nothing). No mechanical gate catches it; CodeRabbit flagged it Major on PR #100. A re-vendor re-emits the empty list. See project_afi_onboard_update_424_traps; the press's compound-workflow resource inference dropping afi's list is a printing-press retro candidate.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For afi the manifest gained: AFI_BASE_URL. server.json gained: AFI_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: AFI_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The afi API resource literally named `resources` never gets a typed table under the framework's reserved catch-all name: from press 4.34 the generator emits none (0.1.x parent-prefixed it to tenants_resources), the full record lives in the generic `resources` table every novel reads, and a 0.1.x store's tenants_resources table is left in place, unused
handfixes.why: afi exposes an API resource literally named `resources`. The press emitted its typed domain table as a bare `resources`, which is the same name as the framework's generic catch-all table. The catch-all CREATE runs first in the migrations slice, so the typed `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "resources"` silently no-ops and every typed insert then runs against the catch-all's column set - failing its NOT NULL `resource_type` on every synced row (`warning: N/N resources items: typed-table upsert failed` on each sync), leaving the typed table permanently empty and polluting the catch-all with a `tenants_id` column it never populates. Scope note, verified against every released store.go (afi-v0.1.0 / afi-v0.1.1 / afi-v0.1.2 - the three afi release tags that exist): the catch-all CREATE winning the race is exactly what makes a typed-shape `resources` table un-writable to disk, so no operator database can carry it and `Open()` was never at risk on a real store; the shape only failed in the generated test fixture, and that behaviour is now pinned by cli/internal/store/legacy_resources_shape_test.go instead of being hidden by the fixture rename. Parent-prefixing to `tenants_resources` is the same disambiguation the generator already applies to `orgs_orgs` / `orgs_tenants`. A reprint re-emits the bare name. See project_afi_onboard_update_424_traps; the press's missing reserved-table-name guard is a printing-press retro candidate. 4.34.2 reprint: the generator absorbed the collision (no typed `resources` table is emitted), so the three tenants_resources store.go asserts are retired and the tests pin the 4.34 shape: exactly one `resources` table, and a 0.1.x tenants_resources table survives an open untouched.

asserts.contains: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND lower(name) = 'resources'

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name; a stored value that repeats a held credential is the shared credential kit's job now (credkit-wiring: every file and SQLite write goes through it); applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. cliutil.RefuseHeld compares each operator-named write with every credential the secret funnel holds, in every view it decodes, and refuses a match before it is written: profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl and the learn tables (learnings, playbooks, candidates, recall misses, entity aliases, patterns). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>. 2026-11-05 kit adoption: the RefuseHeld checks at each store and file (held_persist.go) are retired, replaced by the shared credential kit's file and SQLite sinks; the journal-shape asserts stay. Test: learn/journal_credential_hardening_test.go (the held pass holds through credkit.Hold).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: The Afi API key (raw Authorization header) goes only to the configured base URL (scheme, host, port): AFI_BASE_URL or config base_url, default https://papi.afi.ai. This is now the Origins declaration ({Source: "*", Allowed: base_url}) the shared credential kit's transport enforces on every CLI, novel and MCP client (registerClientHook, credkit_client.go): a request carrying a held value to any other origin is refused, over plain http too, and a redirect hop off that origin is not followed with it.
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the Authorization header to whatever URL it is handed, and Go keeps that header across a redirect to the same host on another port. The connector's own pin (afi_guard.go) is replaced by the kit's Origins check (2026-11-05 kit adoption). internal/credwire/origins_test.go TestKeyGoesOnlyToTheBaseURL drives the built CLI: the key reaches the https base URL as Authorization (control), never follows a 307 to another origin on the same host, and never reaches a plain-http base URL. Scheme, port, apex-domain and look-alike host matching is the kit's own, tested in tools/maintainer/credkit.

handfixes.summary: Afi data names are never credential names: the page_token / next_page_token cursors every list pages with are data, so the Declarations name neither (no ResponseFields entry, no CredentialFields entry), and a paged list, export and sync print and store every page.
handfixes.why: The ported credential layer's token rule would hold every next_page_token a list response carries, so sync, every paged list and the MCP cursor would print withheld after page one. 2026-11-05 kit adoption: the kit holds only declared names, so keeping the cursors out of the Declarations is the fix; the spec-name guard went with the deleted layer. internal/credwire/origins_test.go TestPageTokensAreData: applications --all, export and sync page through a next_page_token, print both pages and withhold nothing, and the cursor reaches the API on every run.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces the print's own credential layer (held set, encodings, output chokepoint, secret funnel, request scan, stream context, outbound and split checks, origin pin, store and journal refusals). internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit (the MCP main at every return of run, so a token-less --transport http launch prints its refusal naming AFI_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and exits non-zero); every API client gets credkit.Transport through the client hook (cli/credkit_client.go), and the feedback and webhook clients build theirs on it; the API key goes only to the configured base URL; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit (WriteFile, AppendFile, OpenFile, NewWriter for export --output); the read-write store opens SQLite through credkit.SQLDriver; the MCP server passes MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP and runs CLI children through RunCommand; TTY state is credkit.Terminal. invitation_url and password are declared response credentials.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies ported from backup-radar, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. The three classes the 4.34.2 print's review left open close through the kit, proved on the built binaries in internal/credwire/classes_test.go: TestOrgsCreateNeverPrintsTheInvitationURL (credential-bearing-url: orgs create on the CLI, with --stdin and over MCP never prints invitation_url; seen failing with invitation_url removed from ResponseFields), TestSplitKeyNeverPrintedOrStored (secret-split-across-fields: the key's base32 halves across two values are withheld on stdout and never reach SQLite; seen failing on the pre-kit tree), TestShortPasswordEmbeddedNeverPrints (short-held-value-embedded: a record with password "qJ" repeated inside another value is withheld; seen failing on the pre-kit tree and with password removed from ResponseFields). TestMalformedConfigCredentialNeverPrints (startup ordering: a key in a config that does not parse is held before Cobra quotes it back) and TestMCPHTTPWithoutTokenRefuses (seen failing on the pre-kit tree: exit 1 with empty stderr). Evidence: .review/failfirst/. Retired entries: _superseded.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (mains, transport hook, file sinks, SQLite driver, MCP framing) and the Declarations literal.

handfixes.summary: export hands the credential kit whole records: no bufio.Writer over stdout, the --deliver tee or the kit file Writer. JSON-lines records are batched by exportRecords (every Write is one or more whole records with their newlines, at most exportBatchBytes = 4 KiB unless one record is larger, written before each page is fetched) and --format json is one Write of the whole document. The table printers go through newTabWriter, a tabwriter over wholeLines, so each table line is one Write. TestNoChunkingWritersOverKitSinks fails on any bufio, csv or bare tabwriter writer, or io.Copy other than into io.Discard, in the module outside the vendored kit.
handfixes.why: Carried from backup-radar's kit adoption (#569), where an executed repro showed the press export's 4096-byte bufio.Writer ended every unit the kit checked inside a record: the kit keeps a JSON document open across units and past its 16 KiB window the stream is lost and every later unit withheld, so an ordinary export stopped after about 20 KiB with exit 74. Whole records close the document at every unit. Test: credwire/export_stream_test.go TestExportStreamsEveryRecord (750 installations, past 64 KiB, paged by next_page_token, to stdout as JSON lines and as JSON, to --output both ways, through --deliver file:, and 550 over MCP: every record, in order, exit 0); cli/whole_records_test.go for the writers and the guard.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the export template should write JSON-lines records whole (no bufio.Writer over the output) and the JSON document in one Write; table output should reach stdout a whole line per Write.

handfixes.summary: A saved run profile's base-url is a credential source: at startup, inside credkit.Start (credentialFiles), holdProfiles reads the current profiles.json under the default home and every --home (cliutil.ConfigDir, so AFI_CONFIG_DIR, AFI_HOME and XDG resolve as profile.go resolves them) and the legacy ~/.afi-cli/profiles.json, member by member so every duplicate key is seen, and holds each base-url value's password and query values through credkit.HoldURL under source profile:base-url. Origins sends that source nowhere, so neither the profile's own host nor the configured base URL becomes an origin for it. The CLI has no credential flag (--credential-ref names a reference), so base-url is the only profile value name held.
handfixes.why: Orchestrator kit rule 8(c): a profile value under a credential flag's name or under base-url is a credential source, held at startup through the kit, every duplicate included. profile.go keeps its own path code (DO NOT EDIT), so the two path asserts below fail a reprint that moves a store, which must then be mirrored in holdProfiles. Tests: credwire/profiles_test.go TestSavedProfileValuesNeverPrint (profile show, use, list and a --profile run print no password or query value, from the --home, AFI_HOME, AFI_CONFIG_DIR and legacy stores, duplicate base-url included) and TestSavedProfileBaseURLIsSentNowhere (a held profile secret is never sent to the configured base URL; a control proves the send path is live). Carried from backup-radar (#569).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated wiring should hold the run profile stores (current and legacy) at startup, as it holds the config and credential store files.

handfixes.why: Publish review round 1 (Codex, kit adoption): the press template starts the browser helper with a raw Start that inherits AFI_API_KEY, configForSave kept the environment's base URL (and any password in it) in config.toml and credentials.toml, and restoreCredentialsFile replayed a 0644 mode. Each has a built-binary or unit test seen failing first.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
